const CTX = `You are one of several agents working for RoofingApp (repo ${REPO}, branch codex/montana-weather-pilot with main merged). The owner (Carson) has chosen the STAGED ROUTE for the "3D storm view": storm layers on the website's Map page first, a globe only later. A supervisor reads your output; it is data, not prose for a person.

Read first: ${REPO}/AGENTS.md (the website rules: Python builds all data and pages; hand-written JavaScript only for browser-only needs, documented; third-party code served by the site; evidence honesty; feeds need a CONTRACTS entry with units, timing, cadence and missing-value rules, changed together with the parser and the tests; verify UI in a real browser; no "best" claims), ${REPO}/docs/DESIGN.md (states loaded/problem/stale, gap words, the text List, phone sizes, "Missing is not dry"), ${REPO}/research/globe/README.md sections 1, 2, 4 and 6 (the staged route: P0 gates and P1 "text first"), and ${EVID}mrms.json (MRMS facts: 33 MergedReflectivityQC levels 00.50…19.00 km above mean sea level, 0.01-degree grid 7000 x 3500 with first point 54.995 N / -129.995 E, 2-minute cadence with 2-second jitter between levels, -99 and -999 are "no radar data" with meanings unverified, 20-25 MB gz per step for all levels, ~0.3-1 MB per level).

Binding rules: never write names of AI models or AI vendors into any file; commit nothing (the supervisor commits); keep every number with its unit and source; wording per rule 5 (radar estimate; no echo is not clear; no "dry", "clear" or "no hail"); no severity ramps; every hazard colour carries its word. Outbound HTTPS works; pip install works but never add a package the website build does not already use (requests, jinja2, pillow, numpy, pygrib, tzdata); downloads go under ${SCRATCH}/storm-dl/<slug>/ and are never committed. Your final output: files changed (paths), commands run with results verbatim, measurements with units, open questions.`

const RECORD = `# Task: record the owner's decision (slug: record-decision). Edit ONLY docs/DECISIONS.md, docs/ROADMAP.md and research/globe/README.md.
1. docs/DECISIONS.md: the D30 entry (written today) says two routes are recorded without a choice. Add, inside D30 after the "Two routes" sentence, one short paragraph in the file's voice: "Decision, 2026-10-17: Carson chose the staged route — storm layers on the Map page first (P1 text values, P2 the Band 13 picture, P3 MESH only with verified units, P4 the echo-top raster, P5 cloud-top classes, P6 a two-hour loop), behind a build flag that is off by default; a link-only globe only after the P4 gate and a separate approval of a vendored library and JavaScript caps." 2. docs/ROADMAP.md Next 16: replace "Two routes, not yet chosen: … (b) …" with the chosen route in one or two lines (route a, with P1 as the first step and the P0 gates named: schedule cadence, counsel on publishing terms before P2, the -99/-999 check, the below-ground share), keeping the item's length.

const P0 = `# Task: measure the P0 gates (slug: p0-gates). Write ONLY ${EVID}p0-gates.json (at most 25 KB) and scripts under ${SCRATCH}/storm-scripts/p0/.
1. Below-ground share of the MRMS 0.5, 0.75, 1.0 and 1.5 km levels across Montana: draw 1,000 points with a fixed seed uniformly over the site's frame box (lat 43.0-50.5, lon -118.5 to -101.0; website/gridded.py line 38) and separately over the view box (44.35-49.01 N, 116.06-104.03 W) and at the 14 towns in website/towns.json; get ground elevation from AWS Terrain Tiles (terrarium PNG, zoom 9 or 10; decode elevation = R*256 + G + B/256 - 32768; cite ${EVID}terrain.json for the format and its Billings check of 953 m); report the share of points whose ground is above 500, 750, 1000 and 1500 m, per box, and the 14 towns' elevations with which levels lie below ground at each. Record bytes downloaded.
2. The meanings of MRMS -99 and -999: retry https://www.nssl.noaa.gov/projects/mrms/operational/tables.php (it returned HTTP 503 earlier) with a plain GET and a browser-like User-Agent; also try the MRMS operational product guide and GRIB2 table PDFs linked from https://www.nssl.noaa.gov/projects/mrms/ and the MRMS entries on https://vlab.noaa.gov/web/wdtd/-/mrms-products and https://inside.nssl.noaa.gov/mrms/ (whatever answers); search for the sentences defining "missing" and "no coverage" (expected: -999 missing, -99 no coverage, or the reverse). Quote exactly with URLs; if nothing authoritative answers, say so and list what was tried (status codes). Do not infer from data.
3. The site's schedule cadence: use the GitHub MCP tools (ToolSearch "select:mcp__github__actions_list") to list ALL completed runs of .github/workflows/website.yml on main with event schedule (page through perPage 100), compute every gap between consecutive scheduled starts over the whole history, the median and p90, the share of 10-minute slots that actually ran, and the runs' durations. Quote the GitHub docs sentences on schedule delays and dropping (${EVID}hosting-options.json has them) and the docs' advice on avoiding the top of the hour if such a sentence exists (fetch https://docs.github.com/en/actions/writing-workflows/choosing-when-your-workflow-runs/events-that-trigger-workflows#schedule and quote). Propose, as text only (do not edit the workflow), an offset cron such as "3-59/10 * * * *" or "7,17,27,37,47,57 * * * *" with the reasoning, and what would prove it works (a 24-hour measurement on main after the change). Note that schedules run only on the default branch, so no branch test exists.
4. Counsel items: list the two clauses the owner's counsel must read (the Actions terms sentences and the GOES file banner) with their quotes from hosting-options.json and goes-aws.json, as data only.
Return the measurements and the file path.`

const P1 = `# Task: implement P1 "text first" (slug: p1-implement). Edit only website/**, tests/**, and .github/workflows/website.yml; create new files where needed. Do not touch research/, docs/, payload/, desktop/.
Read before coding: website/gridded.py in full (MRMS listing, pygrib decode, mrms_grid/mrms_index/sample_mrms, RADAR_STALE = 30 min, the status/problem pattern, how frames are named), website/build.py in full (Collector, towns(), gridded(), map_data() → data/map.json, build() and its flags, the --sample path), website/sources.py (CONTRACTS entries' shape, LIMITS), website/sample.py (how labelled sample data is made), website/templates/map.html and website/static/map/map.js (how the List of towns is rendered — find the seam where town text is produced; prefer Jinja-rendered text; if the List is built in the browser from data/map.json, add the smallest documented change), website/templates/town.html (the town page), website/towns.json (fields; whether towns carry an elevation), tests/test_gridded.py and tests/test_site.py (patterns: synthetic grids, fake fetchers, built-site checks), .github/workflows/website.yml (the unittest line ~84, the branch preview build command, the path filter).
Build:
1. website/storm.py (new, Python only, numpy + pygrib + stdlib + the existing fetcher): list the MRMS bucket for the newest common step of 11 MergedReflectivityQC levels (0.50, 1.00, 2.00, 3.00, 4.00, 5.00, 6.00, 8.00, 10.00, 12.00, 15.00 km — nearest-time join across levels within 10 s, per the jitter fact), download and decode each (pygrib; verify Ni 7000 / Nj 3500 from the message; the level comes from the file name; values in dBZ; -99 and -999 are "no radar data" and must never become a value or 0), sample the 14 towns' cells (reuse gridded.mrms_index), and compute per town: echo_top_m (the highest sampled level with dBZ >= 35, in metres above mean sea level) or None with a reason ("no echo at or above 35 dBZ at the 11 sampled heights" or "no radar data at any sampled height"), max_dbz and its height, valid_levels (count with a dBZ value), no_data_levels (count with -99/-999), below_ground_levels (levels whose height is below the town's ground elevation — add an "elevation_m" to towns.json only if it is missing and you can source it from the NWS points/grid data the build already fetches; otherwise take it from the station grid elevation the Collector already has; state the source in the output), valid_time_utc (the join time), retrieved_utc, and status loaded | problem | stale (stale past RADAR_STALE). Never label anything "no radar coverage" (unverified); use "no radar data". Wording for the List and the town page, from the Collector in Python: e.g. "Echo top (radar estimate): 8,000 m above sea level, valid 2:40 PM MDT; dBZ 35 or more at 4 of 11 sampled heights (2 below ground, 0 with no radar data). This is not an all-clear." and the no-echo case "No echo at or above 35 dBZ at the 11 sampled heights (valid …). This is not an all-clear." — no "dry", "clear", "no hail" strings anywhere.
2. build.py: a --storm-layers flag, default off. Off: the build output must be byte-identical to today's (no storm keys in map.json, no new strings in any page, no extra downloads) — add a test that proves it with the sample fetcher. On: the Collector calls storm.collect(), notes a status line "MRMS reflectivity levels" with ok/detail like the other notes, writes towns[].storm into data/map.json, and renders the text into the List and the town pages via Jinja. --sample must produce labelled SAMPLE storm values (website/sample.py) so offline builds and tests work.
3. sources.py: a CONTRACTS entry "storm_levels" in the file's shape (units dBZ and metres above mean sea level; cadence 2 minutes; the 11 levels; stale after 30 minutes like radar; missing values -99/-999 "no radar data, meanings unverified"; the echo-top rule 35 dBZ; "radar estimate, not observed hail or damage"); it appears on the About page wherever CONTRACTS are rendered.
4. Tests: tests/test_storm.py (offline, synthetic 11-level stacks and a fake fetcher): echo top chosen correctly; sentinels never a value or 0; below-ground counted and excluded; nearest-time join; the no-echo reason; stale status past 30 min; no forbidden strings in the rendered text; valid_levels + no_data_levels = 11. tests/test_site.py additions: with --storm-layers and sample data, 14 of 14 towns show a value or a named reason in the List and on the town pages, every value carries "radar estimate", "above sea level" and a valid time; without the flag the built site has no "Echo top" string and map.json has no "storm" key. Add tests.test_storm to the unittest line in website.yml and pass --storm-layers in the BRANCH preview build only (not the main publish), so branch pushes exercise it live.
5. Run: python -m unittest discover -s tests (all must pass), python -m website.build --out ${SCRATCH}/_site_off --sample and --storm-layers --sample into ${SCRATCH}/_site_on, then diff the two trees (only the storm additions may differ), then one live run: python -m website.build --out ${SCRATCH}/_site_live --require-live --storm-layers (record bytes downloaded for the 11 levels, decode seconds, and the 14 towns' values as text). If the live run finds no echo anywhere (likely in October), say so and show the no-echo wording. Do not run a browser check (the supervisor will push the branch for the Website preview).
Return: files changed, the exact new wording strings, the test command and result, the sizes and timings, and open questions (for instance where elevation came from).`

const REVIEW = (p1) => `# Task: adversarial review of the P1 change (slug: p1-review). Do not edit any file; write ${EVID}p1-review.json (at most 20 KB).
The implementer reported: ${JSON.stringify(p1).slice(0, 6000)}
Run cd ${REPO} && git status --short && git diff -- website tests .github | head -2000 to read the whole diff (use git diff with paths if it is long; read new files in full). Check against: AGENTS.md rules 4-9 and the conventions; DESIGN.md states and words; README §4 evidence rules and §6 P1 done-when ("14 of 14 towns show a value or a named reason; no dry or no hail string; each value carries radar estimate, metres above sea level and valid time; any value without its valid-column count is removed"); the byte-identical requirement with the flag off; the CONTRACTS entry's completeness (units, timing, cadence, missing values) and that the About page renders it; sentinel handling (-99/-999 never a value, never 0, never "no radar coverage"); the nearest-time join; stale logic (30 min); the elevation source and below-ground arithmetic; sample data labelled SAMPLE; the workflow change (tests added; flag only on branch previews; main publish unchanged); test quality (do the tests fail if the behaviour breaks? try mutating one rule mentally); JavaScript added (lines, documented, browser-only?); phone layout risk of the new text; anything that could make the main build fail or slower by more than 60 s. Default to suspicion. Output JSON: {"blocking": [{"file", "line", "what", "fix"}], "should_fix": [...], "nits": [...], "verified_ok": [...], "tests_run": [{"command", "result"}]} and return its summary.`

const FIX = (review) => `# Task: apply the review and verify (slug: p1-fix-verify). Edit only website/**, tests/**, .github/workflows/website.yml.
Review findings: ${JSON.stringify(review).slice(0, 8000)}
Apply every "blocking" and "should_fix" item (and nits that are cheap). Then run and record verbatim: cd ${REPO} && python -m unittest discover -s tests 2>&1 | tail -3 ; python -m website.build --out ${SCRATCH}/_site_off2 --sample ; python -m website.build --out ${SCRATCH}/_site_on2 --sample --storm-layers ; diff -rq ${SCRATCH}/_site_off2 ${SCRATCH}/_site_on2 (list differing files; only storm additions may differ); python -m website.build --out ${SCRATCH}/_site_live2 --require-live --storm-layers (exit code, bytes, seconds, the 14 towns' storm text lines); python desktop/launcher.py --selftest payload | tail -1. Then a browser check of the built live site with the Playwright venv described in ${EVID}webgl-runtime.json "recipe" (or tools/smoke_map.py's own way of launching Chromium): serve ${SCRATCH}/_site_live2 with python -m http.server on a free port, open map.html and one town page at 288 px and 1440 px widths, assert no sideways scroll (scrollWidth equals innerWidth), assert the echo-top text is visible in the List and on the town page, save screenshots under ${SCRATCH}/storm-shots/ (not the repo). Record pass/fail per check. Write ${EVID}p1-verification.json (at most 20 KB) with the commands, results, timings and screenshots' paths. Return the summary and anything still failing with the exact error.`

log('Staged route: recording the decision, measuring P0 gates, building P1 in parallel')
const [rec, p0, p1] = await parallel([
  () => agent(CTX + '\n\n' + RECORD, { label: 'record-decision', phase: 'Decision + P0 + P1 build', model: 'haiku' }),
  () => agent(CTX + '\n\n' + P0, { label: 'p0-gates', phase: 'Decision + P0 + P1 build', model: 'haiku' }),
  () => agent(CTX + '\n\n' + P1, { label: 'p1-implement', phase: 'Decision + P0 + P1 build', model: 'haiku' }),
])
log('Reviewing the P1 diff')
const review = await agent(CTX + '\n\n' + REVIEW(p1), { label: 'p1-review', phase: 'Review', model: 'haiku' })
log('Applying the review and verifying')
const fix = await agent(CTX + '\n\n' + FIX(review), { label: 'p1-fix-verify', phase: 'Fix and verify', model: 'haiku' })
return { rec, p0, p1, review, fix }
